title: E2ER structured review
description: What one paper claims, in a form another program can read. Every claim carries the verbatim sentence it was taken from, so a reader can check it against the source rather than trusting the extractor. Written by `e2er corpus add`; verified offline by verify_review(). Published as a portable format any extractor could emit and any consumer could read.

schema_version.description: Which contract this record follows. The only required field: everything else degrades gracefully, but a consumer that cannot tell which version it is reading cannot degrade safely.

paper_id.description: Identifier within the producing system. Not portable; use doi to match across corpora.

doi.description: Bare DOI, no https://doi.org/ prefix, lowercased. The deduplication key.

source.description: Where the record came from: openalex, arxiv, semantic_scholar, crossref, zotero, local_pdf, ...

access_license.description: License of the full text the claims were extracted from, when known. Empty means unknown, which is not the same as unrestricted.

extracted_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of the extraction.

extractor_model.description: Model that produced the claims. Recorded because extraction quality is a property of the model, and a corpus mixing models should say so.

source_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the NORMALISED source text (whitespace collapsed, soft hyphenation removed, smart quotes folded — see normalize() in review.py). Normalised rather than raw so the same PDF read by two different extractors fingerprints identically.

verification.description: Optional. The verdict reached on this record. Always recomputable from (record, source text), so a consumer may ignore it; stored because the rejections are evidence about the extractor rather than about the paper.

evidence.title: Evidence
evidence.description: The sentence a claim was taken from, and where it was found.

quote.description: A VERBATIM span from the source text. Not a paraphrase, not a tidied quote. Verification locates it by exact substring match after normalisation; a quote shorter than 24 characters is rejected outright, because a short fragment matches text it never came from.

locator.description: Human hint for finding the quote: section heading, page, table number. Never used for matching.

char_start.description: Offset of the quote in the normalised source text. -1 means not located.

verified.description: Whether the quote was found. A record whose claims are all false here has been checked and failed, which is not the same as unchecked.

reason.description: Why verification failed, when it did. Empty when verified.

claim.title: Claim
claim.description: One extracted statement plus the evidence for it. `text` is the extractor's paraphrase and is never treated as fact on its own; `evidence.quote` is what makes it checkable.

nullableClaim.description: null means the field was not extracted, or was extracted and rejected. Absence of a claim is never evidence that the paper lacks one.

passed.description: rejected == 0. True vacuously when total == 0, which is why `conclusive` exists.

conclusive.description: total > 0. An extraction that produced nothing passes without having checked anything, and must not read like one that checked twenty claims.

rejections.description: One entry per claim that failed, retained after the claim itself is dropped. This is the measurement: how often an extractor invents a quote when it has been told the quote will be checked.

field.description: Which review field the rejected claim belonged to.
